{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are a vulnerability analyst. Input JSON has "system_profile" (installed software with versions, in varied formats: 'Product Name X.Y.Z', 'vendor/product@version', 'vendor-product X.Y', 'vendor product X.Y.Z.W') and "advisories" (each with "id", "description", "affected" giving product and version constraints, e.g. "vendor/product: version < 3.0.0", "version >= 1.0 and <= 2.5", "version = 7.15", multiple constraints joined by OR). For each advisory, decide whether it applies to the installed system.

Work through EVERY advisory against EVERY installed product. Do not skip any advisory; do not return an empty list unless you have explicitly verified that none applies — most inputs contain several applicable advisories, and an empty answer is almost certainly an error. Also do not pad the answer: an advisory belongs in the output only if BOTH product match AND version constraint hold; including advisories for products that are not installed or whose version is outside the affected range is a serious error.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCHING. Normalize both the advisory's product name and every installed product name: lowercase, strip separators (spaces, '-', '_', '/', '@'). The same product may appear in different styles: 'Blackberry Athoc' ~ 'blackberry/athoc'; 'elastic elastic cloud enterprise' ~ 'elastic/elastic_cloud_enterprise'; 'dexgate' ~ 'dexma/dexgate'; 'phpgurukul/job_portal@1.0' ~ 'phpgurukul job portal 1.0'; 'Jetbrains Youtrack 2023.1.16597.1' ~ 'jetbrains/youtrack'; 'lock_screen 9.0.17' ~ 'lenovo/lock_screen'. Match if the names are identical after normalization, or identical after removing the vendor prefix from one or both sides, or one is a clear alias (spacing/hyphenation/case differences, Title Case vs lowercase, package-manager style vs display name). They must be the SAME actual software — not merely similar or sharing a vendor. A vendor-stripped installed name IS a match. A name appearing only in the advisories but nowhere in system_profile (directly or by alias) is NOT installed — never include those.

STEP 2 — VERSION PARSING AND COMPARISON. Extract the version from each installed entry (the trailing numeric token sequence; formats like '@version', ' X.Y.Z', ' X.Y.Z.W' all count). Parse as dot-separated numeric segments; compare segment by segment numerically (10 > 9; 2023.1.10 > 2023.1.4; 20230607 is one number). Trailing zero segments are padding: 7.15.0 == 7.15, 8.31.0.0 == 8.31.0, 4.0.20.0 == 4.0.20, 9.1.6.0 == 9.1.6. If the installed version has more segments than the bound, compare up to the bound's depth after trimming trailing zeros from the installed version; if the compared segments are equal and the bound has no more segments, the versions are equal only when the extra installed segments are all zeros — otherwise the installed version is greater. E.g. 2023.1.16597.1 > 2023.1; 1.0.0.0.1 > 1.1.0.0 bound at depth 4 is 1.0.0.0 vs 1.1.0.0 → less.

STEP 3 — BOUNDARY SEMANTICS. Evaluate each bound individually and exactly, using the structured "affected" field (never the description prose for version logic; but when "affected" uses prose like "versions prior to B are affected" or "from A before B", parse it as: 'prior to B' → installed < B; 'from A before B' → installed >= A and < B):
- "version < B": affected only if installed is STRICTLY less than B. Installed == B is NOT affected; installed == B.0 or B.0.0 is also NOT affected (padding zeros make it equal). E.g. installed 8.31.0.0 vs "< 8.31.0" → NOT affected; installed 4.0.20.1 vs "< 4.0.20.0" → NOT affected (greater); installed 20230607.0 vs "< 20230607" → NOT affected; installed 1.1 vs "< 1.1" → NOT affected. But installed 9.0.17 vs "< 9.0.18" → affected; installed 5.5.3 vs "<= 5.5.3" → affected; installed 23.0.0 vs ">= 23.0.0 and < 23.1.0" → affected.
- "version <= B": affected if installed is less than OR EQUAL to B. Installed == B or B.0 IS affected.
- "version = B": affected only if numerically equal, treating padding zeros as equal (7.15.0 matches bound 7.15; 7.15.1 does not; 757 matches 757; 300 matches 300; 4.0.1.0 matches 4.0.1).
- "version > B" / ">= B": strict / inclusive respectively.
- Ranges ">= A and <= B" or ">= A and < B": EVERY AND-ed part must hold. "< B" excludes B itself; "<= B" includes it. E.g. installed 11.1.9 vs ">= 11.1.0 and <= 11.1.9" → affected; installed 3.0.0.0 vs ">= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2" → affected; installed 8.6.10 vs ">= 8.6.0 and <= 8.6.5" → NOT affected (above the upper bound); installed 8.11.1.1 vs ">= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1" → NOT affected (greater at depth 4); installed 7.0.0.1 vs ">= 7.0.0 and <= 7.0.6" → affected; installed 1.0.0.100 vs ">= 1.0.0.95 and < 1.0.0.100" → NOT affected (equals exclusive bound).
- Multiple constraints joined by OR (which may name different products, e.g. "nozominetworks/cmc: ... OR nozominetworks/guardian: ..."): the advisory applies if the installed product matches one named product AND that complete constraint is satisfied by its version.

STEP 4 — DECISION. An advisory is applicable iff (a) its product matches an installed product AND (b) the installed version satisfies at least one complete constraint. Do not include advisories for products not installed. Do not include advisories whose constraint excludes the installed version — check especially versions exactly at an exclusive bound (with trailing zeros), versions above a range's upper bound, and versions one patch above an exact-equality bound. But DO include the many advisories whose product is installed and whose version IS below the bound — a lower installed version like 9.0.17 under "< 9.0.18", or 5.10.0.0 vs "prior to 5.10.1"-style bounds, is affected. Do not drop applicable advisories merely because the product name style differs (Title Case vs vendor/product) or the bound is written as prose; convert prose bounds per Step 3.

STEP 5 — OUTPUT. Collect the "id" of every applicable advisory, verbatim and unique, and return ONLY the JSON object {"applicable_cves":["CVE-...", ...]} with no additional text, markdown, or code fences. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.

Before answering, re-verify: (1) every product match including vendor-stripped, alias, and Title Case/package-manager forms; (2) every boundary comparison, especially '<' vs '<=' at exact-boundary versions and exact-equality constraints where the installed version has trailing zeros; (3) that you enumerated every advisory one by one and committed to a match/no-match decision for each. Enumerate all advisories, then write the final list only after all are
